verses.t: In those days the fallen mal'akim came down, and they knew the secrets of all things. At this time sin was great in the earth and the earth was filled with violence, and they killed many people, and they begat giants with mortal women.

The wicked mal'akim consumed everything that the earth produced and they consumed the great fish and the birds of the sky with all that grew and they ate the fruit of the earth and all kinds of grain and all the trees they devoured.

Beasts and reptiles they sinned against, and all creeping things of the earth and they observed all earthly things; every harsh deed and harsh utterance upon male and female, and among humans as well.

The two hundred mal'akim seized two hundred donkeys, two hundred asses, two hundred sheep and rams of the flock, two hundred goats, two hundred of every beast of the field from every animal, from every bird they took them for in-breeding with humans, for miscegenation (inbreeding of people considered to be of different races) of every kind.

Then the fallen ones came, and they defiled all creation, and they begot giants and monsters upon the earth. These were the ones whom they begot, and, behold, all the earth was corrupted and was defiled with its blood and by the hand of the giants which did not satisfy them and they turned against mankind, and they were seeking to devour many more, and the monsters attacked it.

The monsters sought out flesh which would be destroyed or perverted. All the monsters and giants will be destroyed, though they would arise in their might, lacking in true knowledge of Aluahim, because they were abominations, and the earth grew corrupt and the giants more mighty upon it, and they were considering the mishpat that would come from the mal'akim upon them.
In the end it will perish and die for they caused great corruption in the earth yet this did not suffice to satisfy them, and it was said: "they will be destroyed from the face of the earth."

Mahway reported that in his dream they drenched the tablet in the water and the waters went up over the tablet then they lifted out the tablet from the water of the flood, and all the names but three had vanished.
And the group said: this vision is for cursing and sorrow.
I am the one who confessed and who will be blamed most of the whole group of the castaways that I shall go to hear the ruchot of the slain complaining about their killers and crying out and saying

That we shall die together and be made an end of together, for our wickedness is much and I will be sleeping, and bread will be denied me for my dwelling; the vision and also the monsters, troubled by it, entered into the gathering of the giants and troubled them.
Then came Ohya and he said to Mahway Tell me the vision without trembling.
Who showed you all this vision, my brother? And Mahway said: Baraqal, my father, was with me.
And Before Mahway had finished telling what he had seen Ohya said to him, Now I have heard wonders! If a barren woman gives birth then this too may come to pass.
Thereupon Ohya said to Hahya We are about to be destroyed from upon the earth and removed from the earth. When they heard this, they wept before the giants and mourned.
Use your strength the group counselled. After that, Ohya said to Hahya Who has done this to us? Then he answered, It is not for us, but for Azazal, for he did show the most corruption to mankind.
the children of mal'akim are the giants, and they would not let all their proved ones be neglected But we have not been cast down; you have strength and can resist.
And Gilgamesh said: I am a giant, and by the mighty strength of my arm and my own great strength I can overcome any one mortal, and I have made war against them; but I am not now
Able to stand against them, for my opponents are mal'akim who reside in Shamayim, and they dwell in the qadash (Set Apart) places.
And not only that, but they are stronger than I.
The day of the wild beast has come, and the wild man they call me.

And they were silent. Then Ohya said to him, I have been forced to have a dream and the sleep of my eyes vanished, to let me see a vision. Now I know that on the field of battle we cannot win, I nor Gilgamesh himself.
Three of its roots remained, while I was watching, there came beings from shamayim, and they moved the roots into this garden, all of them, and not the three.

Concerns the death of our nepheshoth said Ohya, and of Gilgamesh and all his comrades, and Ohya told them what Gilgamesh said to him in the night, and it was said that all the forebodings were "concerning the rulers of the earth, for the leader has cursed the potentates" and the giants were glad at his words. Then he turned and left the qahal.

Thereupon two of them had dreams and the sleep of their eye, fled from them, and they arose and came to the gathering of the giants and told their dreams, and said in the qahal of their comrades the monsters saying:
In my dream I was watching this very night and there was a garden and in it were gardeners and they were watering the garden, and

two hundred trees and large shoots came out of their root and suddenly the garden was ablaze, and it consumed all the water, and the fire burned all the garden and nothing was left. They found the giants to tell them the dream but none could interpret it.
Then one said: Let us go to Ḥanoḵ the noted scribe, and he will interpret for us the dream.

Thereupon his fellow Ohya declared and said to the giants, I too had a dream this night, O giants, and, behold, the Ruler of Shamayim came down to earth and thrones were set up, and the Great Qadash One sat, and the books were opened, and he made an end of us; and such is the end of the dream.
Thereupon all the giants and monsters grew afraid and called Mahway.
He came to them and the giants pleaded with him and sent him to Ḥanoḵ, the noted scribe.
They said to him, Go to Ḥanoḵ, so that it may be known to you that he has spoken with you, and that you have heard his voice.
And he said to him, He will listen and interpret the dreams and tell us how long the giants have to live. And Mahway went.

Then he mounted up in the air like strong ruchot, and flew with his hands like eagles and he left behind the inhabited world and passed over Desolation, the great desert and came to the dwelling of Ḥanoḵ,

And Ḥanoḵ saw him and hailed him, and Mahway said to him of his mission, and said he would speak with him. Flying hither and thither a second time to Mahway came Ḥanoḵ. And Mahway said: The giants await your words, and all the monsters of the earth.

If the fall of the giants has been carried out from the days of their esteem, tell us whether their days and they will be added to our lives; we would know from you their meaning concerning the two hundred trees that from shamayim came down and the three shoots that remained.
And the voice said: "for the closed door of the sun will open, the sun's light and heat will descend and set your wings alight.
You will burn and die," said he.
Having heard these words, I beat my wings and quickly flew down from the air.
I looked back: Dawn had broken, and with the light of the sun it had come to rise over the Kögmän mountains.
And again a voice came from above.

Bringing the command of Ḥanoḵ, the apostle, it said: "I call you, Virōgdād (Baraqal), come down; I know your errand and his direction is upon you go, you and do not tarry. Now quickly go down to the people and to Ḥanoḵ also deliver your message."

The scribe Ḥanoḵ wrote a copy of the second tablet that Ḥanoḵ sent written in the very handwriting of Ḥanoḵ the noted scribe thus: In the name of Aluahim the great and qadash (Set Apart One), to SemYahza and all his companions greeting: let it be known to you that not only for the works of your hands shall you be judged, but for and the things you have done, and that your wives shall not escape;
They and their sons and the wives of their sons will not escape, for they were defiled by your licentiousness on the earth, and there has been upon you a heavenly mishpat.
and the land is crying out and complaining about you and the deeds of your children and the harm that you have done to it.
Your mishpat is held back only until Raphaal arrives, behold, destruction is coming, a great flood, and it will destroy all living things and whatever is in the deserts and the seas.
And the meaning of the matter is a mishpat that has come upon you for evil.
But now, loosen the bonds binding you to evil and turn, and pray.
And great fear seized me and I fell on my face; I heard his voice saying of Ḥanoḵ that he dwelt among human beings but he did not learn from them or rely on them.
Then the battle grew hard and every arrow was fitted to the bow, he that shot it was slain. Sām said: "Baruk be the one who escaped; had he seen this, he would not have died."
Then Shahmīzād said to Sām, his son: "All that Māhawai has done is spoilt."

Thereupon he said to Sām: "We are bound until the day of mishpat, and like those that are in the fiery Sheol for ever. As my father, Virōgdād, was told, so it shall be." Shahmīzād said: "It is true what he says. He says one of thousands. For one of thousands shall escape".
Sām thereupon began to search for Māhawai, too, in many places he sought, until to that place he might escape and hide.
Then Virōgdād was angry, and Hōbābīš robbed Ahr … of his wife.
Thereupon the giants began to kill each other and to abduct their wives.
The creatures, too, began to kill each other.

Sām stood before the sun, one hand in the air, the other upon the earth; and whatever he obtained, to his brother he gave. And he was imprisoned and his cry went over To the mal'akim a word came down from shamayim. To Sām, who took the tablet and threw (or: was thrown) into the water.
Finally Sām in his sleep saw three signs, one portending battle, one woe and flight, and one utter annihilation.
Narīmān saw a garden full of trees in rows. Two hundred Watchers came out, the trees of the garden.
Then Ḥanoḵ, the apostle, came and gave a message to the demons and their children: To you there is not shalom.
The mishpat on you is that you shall be bound for the sins you have committed.

You shall see the destruction of your children. Ruling for a hundred and twenty years and after the flood the earth shall bring forth wild ass, ibex the ram, goat, gazelle, and oryx, of each two hundred, a pair shall come forth;
The other wild beasts, birds, and animals and their wine shall be six thousand jugs and the irritation of water shall be abundant, and their oil shall be plentiful.

In the house of the father and the nuptials were held until the completion of his days, and in fighting they grew strong, and in the nest Ohya and Ahya were together, and he said to his brother: "get up and let us go; we will take what our father has ordered us to. The pledge we have given is for battle."
And the giants gathered together and said: "Not the roar of the lion, but the strength on his neck. Not the colours of the rainbow, but the bow held firm.
Not the sharpness of the blade, but the strength of the ox. Not the flight of the eagle, but his wings.
Not the shining gold, but the brass that hammers it.
Not the proud ruler, but the diadem on his head.
Not the splendid cypress, but the rock of the mountain beneath it.
… Not he that engages in quarrels, but he that is true in his speech.
Not the evil fruit, but the poison in it.
Not they that are placed in the skies but the Aluahim of all worlds.
Not the servant is proud, but the master that is above him.
Not one that is sent is great, but the man that sent him".

Thereupon Narīmān rose and said I saw in my dream those who were judged. And in another place I saw those that were weeping for the ruin that had befallen them, and whose cries and laments rose up to shamayim.
And also I saw another place where there were tyrants and rulers of the earth in great number, who had lived in sin and evil deeds, when the mishpat came upon them.

And in those days many of the sons of men were killed, four hundred thousand Righteous were slain with fire, naphtha, and brimstone and the earth was laid waste. And the mal'akim veiled or: covered, or: protected, or: moved out of sight Ḥanoḵ.
Chose and extracted and listened to the daughters of men and ravished them.
They chose beautiful women, and demanded of their fathers them in marriage.
Sordid were their deeds; all that they wanted they carried off and severally they were subjected to tasks and services.
And they took men from each city of the land, and were, ordered to serve the Watchers. The Mesenians were directed to prepare, the Khūzians to sweep and water, the Persians to bring them bread.
